exposure: Lower uterine segment (LUS) thickness via 2D transvaginal ultrasound
outcome: Intraoperative classification of LUS thickness (grades I-IV)
Comparison/agreement between ultrasound LUS thickness and intraoperative LUS thickness
cohort: The study included 40 pregnant women with a history of previous cesarean section (C/S) referred to Izadi Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital in Qom, who underwent transvaginal ultrasound followed by C/S.
finding: The mean LUS thickness measured by ultrasound significantly differed between the three grades detected by the gynecologist, indicating that transvaginal ultrasound could be helpful in evaluating the risk of scar dehiscence and uterine rupture in women with LUS grades I and II with a history of previous C/S.
mod_finding: The study compared LUS thickness measurements from ultrasound with intraoperative findings during cesarean section in women with a history of previous C/S, supporting the use of transvaginal ultrasound for assessing scar risk in these cases.
cross-section timing: Third trimester of pregnancy, with ultrasound performed within one week prior to cesarean section.
